selected.title: fix(server): lock operator generation state transitions
selected.author: Afloat16
selected.full_inventory_search_source: Complete disjoint created-date-partitioned closed-author PR search, merged_at present.
selected.summary_en: Serialize operator retries and cancellations with concurrent generation-state transitions.
selected.summary_zh: 通过行锁协调操作员重试、取消与并发生成状态变更。
selected.technical_value: Re-reads the scoped generation job under the same PostgreSQL row lock used by generation completion, evaluates the transition and updates state within one transaction. Queue operations and audit publication occur after that transaction.
selected.test_evidence: Committed PostgreSQL integration fixtures use isolated schemas, real row locks, gated concurrent requests and lock-wait inspection. They cover retry conflicts after processing or completion, duplicate retries, cancellation racing with completion and simultaneous cancellations.
selected.limitations: The integration suite requires CLAUDE_MEM_TEST_POSTGRES_URL and skips when it is absent. No database-backed test was executed during this review. Queue I/O remains outside the row-lock transaction.
selected.selection_reason: Addresses concurrent state mutation through transactional row-lock discipline, with explicit race-oriented integration fixtures.
selected.review_method: Inspected the exact final merge-commit production and regression-test patches. Test evidence is from committed fixtures, without a fresh execution.
selected.selection_refresh: Newer substantial merge from this project's current batch.

selected.title: fix(restore): refuse newer-schema snapshots before swapping live data
selected.author: Afloat16
selected.full_inventory_search_source: Complete disjoint created-date-partitioned closed-author PR search, merged_at present.
selected.summary_en: Reject newer-schema restore snapshots before replacing the healthy live database.
selected.summary_zh: 在替换正常运行的数据库前，拒绝超出当前支持版本的恢复快照。
selected.technical_value: Checks the staged snapshot's PRAGMA user_version against LATEST_SCHEMA_VERSION in the SQLite file-job process before checkpointing or backing up the live database. The staged WAL participates in the compatibility check.
selected.test_evidence: Committed SQLite fixtures verify rejection preserves the live and snapshot bytes, creates no pre-restore copy, leaves a failed pending restore recoverable by the worker and detects a newer schema stamp in the WAL. Older, current and unstamped snapshots remain accepted.
selected.limitations: The preflight checks the schema version stamp and existing SQLite integrity path. This review inspected the fixtures and did not run the restore suite.
selected.selection_reason: Prevents a destructive ordering error in the restore workflow and validates both refusal and compatible-snapshot controls.
selected.review_method: Inspected the exact final merge-commit production and regression-test patches. Test evidence is from committed fixtures, without a fresh execution.
selected.selection_refresh: Newer substantial merge from this project's current batch.

selected.title: fix(sync): remove replica vectors after remote tombstones
selected.author: Afloat16
selected.full_inventory_search_source: Complete disjoint created-date-partitioned closed-author PR search, merged_at present.
selected.summary_en: Schedule replica-vector cleanup after committed remote deletions and earlier writes finish.
selected.summary_zh: 远端删除提交且同条目的先前写入完成后，清理副本中的向量片段。
selected.technical_value: Captures the replica's local row ID before deleting a tombstoned origin record, dispatches cleanup only after the SQLite transaction commits and orders it after earlier writes for that row. Local and replicated deletions share a serialized cleanup lane.
selected.test_evidence: Committed fixtures cover observations, summaries and prompts, assert the replica row ID and matching document type, delay an earlier write to test ordering, discard cleanup on rollback and verify a simulated vector-service failure preserves durable sync progress and permits later cleanup.
selected.limitations: Vector cleanup is best effort. Failures are logged and durable synchronization continues, so a failed vector-service deletion can leave fragments until a later cleanup. Tests use an in-memory SQLite store and a simulated vector client, and were not rerun.
selected.selection_reason: Fixes stale search fragments caused by replicated deletions while explicitly covering transaction rollback and write/delete ordering.
selected.review_method: Inspected the exact final merge-commit production and regression-test patches. Test evidence is from committed fixtures, without a fresh execution.
selected.selection_refresh: Newer substantial merge from this project's current batch.

pr.title: Preserve target Q history and evaluation mode during conversion
pr.author: Afloat16

adopted_commit.author: Afloat16
adopted_commit.message:
Preserve target Q history and evaluation mode during conversion

WorldModel.to() calls init(), which recreated the target Q parameters
from the online ensemble (discarding Polyak/checkpoint history) and
rebuilt the target module in whatever train/eval mode the online
ensemble was in. Initialize the target parameters only once and keep
the target module in eval mode after every rebuild.

Cherry-picked from #98 (implementation only; tests omitted).

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5.1 <noreply@anthropic.com>

files.patch:
@@ -38,7 +38,8 @@ def __init__(self, cfg):
 	def init(self):
 		# Create params
 		self._detach_Qs_params = TensorDictParams(self._Qs.params.data, no_convert=True)
-		self._target_Qs_params = TensorDictParams(self._Qs.params.data.clone(), no_convert=True)
+		if not hasattr(self, "_target_Qs_params"):
+			self._target_Qs_params = TensorDictParams(self._Qs.params.data.clone(), no_convert=True)
 
 		# Create modules
 		with self._detach_Qs_params.data.to("meta").to_module(self._Qs.module):
@@ -51,6 +52,7 @@ def init(self):
 		self._detach_Qs.__dict__["params"] = self._detach_Qs_params
 		delattr(self._target_Qs, "params")
 		self._target_Qs.__dict__["params"] = self._target_Qs_params
+		self._target_Qs.train(False)
 
 	def __repr__(self):
 		repr = 'TD-MPC2 World Model\n'

other_accepted.maintainer_pr_description:
Supersedes #1140, #1141, #1142, #1143, #1144, #1145 and #1146 by @Afloat16. Each one edits `docs/ROADMAP.md` and `docs/STATUS.md`, so merging them one at a time would have left each later one in conflict. They're merged together here with the author's commits kept.

- #1140: inline source-map data URLs ignore their fragment, and the scheme and `base64` marker are matched case-insensitively.
- #1141: ZIP directories are recognised from DOS and Unix attributes even without a trailing slash.
- #1142: rejected ASAR names count toward the listing limit.
- #1143: a HAR with a UTF-8 BOM parses.
- #1144: a .NET bundle member can't read into the manifest's bytes.
- #1145: Play can start a Python project's one installed `[project.scripts]` console script from its own environment.
- #1146: Godot and Electron get an absolute project path.

Two fixes on top of the merge:
- #1145 and #1146 each edited the New-project toolchains row in STATUS. It's now one row carrying both additions, not two copies.
- #1146's `launch_tests` module is moved to the end of `outputs.rs`. On Windows an item after it made clippy fail with `items_after_test_module`, which the Linux gate doesn't compile.

**Verified:** the `formats` and `engine` tests (552 in the engine library), clippy for both on Windows, fmt, `cargo xtask wasm` and layers pass on the merged result.

maintainer_acknowledgment.author: danyaberezun
maintainer_acknowledgment.body: Thanks @Afloat16 — the literal-filename fix landed as part of #1137, credited to you as co-author. #1137 rewrote the same `ignoredPaths` function (a fast `--no-index` first pass), so we folded your fix in there rather than merge two competing versions: the first pass reads `./<path>` records from `--stdin -z`, and the index pass keeps arguments (one index scan per batch — `--stdin` rescans the index per path, ~3× slower on large repos) and unquotes git's C-quoted names, so `"`, `\`, control characters and pathspec-looking names stay literal. Your tests for those names came along. Closing this in favour of #1137.

other_accepted.limitations: The final implementation differs from the source PR: the no-index pass uses NUL-delimited stdin, while the index pass uses bounded arguments and C-quoted path decoding. The entire watcher optimization and its performance results are not attributed to Afloat16. No tests were rerun.

pr.title: [PR] chore(branch): land 40 single-purpose fixes as one history-preserving batch (wave 5)
pr.author: ranxianglei
pr.body:
## What

One history-preserving batch landing Afloat16's 40 open single-purpose fix branches (each was a 1-commit PR with its own hermetic test). Each branch is pulled in as a real merge commit — original authors, commit messages, and history stay intact; no squashing, no cherry-pick rewrites.

Merge order follows the review sequence; the one textual conflict (`scripts/live-files.mjs`, two adjacent live-file registrations) is resolved as the union of both entries.

## Contents (branch → issue)

| Branch | Issue | One-line |
|---|---|---|
| 2026-11-12_apig-canonical-query (#6484) | #6483 | APiG canonical query normalization |
| 2026-11-12_bounded-log-window (#6487) | #6486 | bounded log read window |
| 2026-11-12_async-zstd-decode (#6489) | #6488 | async zstd decode (no sync decompress on hot path) |
| 2026-11-12_reconcile-long-history (#6492) | #6490 | gap-bracket reconcile for 150K-msg histories + spread-arg fix |
| 2026-11-12_search-unicode-offsets (#6494) | #6493 | unicode-safe lowercase-span → original offsets |
| 2026-11-12_cache-diff-byte-offsets (#6496) | #6495 | byte→UTF-16 offset mapping in wire diff |
| 2026-11-12_foreign-sweep-failure-exit (#6498) | #6497 | sweep exits 1 when foreign blocks fail |
| 2026-11-12_drop-fields-own-paths (#6500) | #6499 | hasOwn on compat-drop walks |
| 2026-11-12_inline-null-response-bodies (#6502) | #6501 | null body for HEAD/204/205/304 |
| 2026-11-12_inline-request-abort-signal (#6504) | #6503 | dispatcher falls back to Request input signal |
| 2026-11-13_inline-body-cancel (#6556) | #6555 | signal propagation through Request rebuilds |
| 2026-11-13_pi-inline-abort (#6560) | #6558 | rethrow AbortError before direct fallback |
| 2026-11-13_inline-request-init (#6563) | #6562 | standard Fetch signal-strip semantics in toInlineReq |
| 2026-11-13_pi-inline-fallback (#6566) | #6565 | fallback rebuilds Request, no double FormData |
| 2026-11-13_inline-stream-cancel (#6571) | #6570 | InlineRes bodyStream cancel destroys socket |
| 2026-11-13_inline-signal-cleanup (#6575) | #6573 | detach listeners on finish/close |
| 2026-11-13_proxy-connect-close (#6577) | #6576 | CONNECT error before headers, no 10s wait |
| 2026-11-13_linear-terminal-sse (#6579) | #6578 | O(n) terminal SSE parse, no whole-buffer concat |
| 2026-11-13_tool-content-order (#6581) | #6580 | capToolOutput keeps original part order |
| 2026-11-13_proxy-ca-trust (#6583) | #6582 | undici requestTls/proxyTls CA wiring |
| 2026-11-13_inline-data-billing (#6585) | #6584 | snake_case inline_data billing |
| 2026-11-13_bounded-message-previews (#6593) | #6590 | O(110) session preview walk |
| 2026-11-13_proxy-connect-buffered-data (#6595) | #6594 | paused-mode CONNECT reply read, no byte loss |
| 2026-11-13_lazy-message-stringify (#6597) | #6596 | JSON.stringify only when echo predicate matches |
| 2026-11-13_fastpath-json-grammar (#6599) | #6598 | strict JSON grammar in fastpath scan |
| 2026-11-13_multiline-sse-rewrite (#6603) | #6600 | multi-data: SSE frame join before rewrite |
| 2026-11-13_reactivation-linear (#6604) | #6601 | linear reactivation |
| 2026-11-13_egress-header-isolation (#6606) | #6605 | case-insensitive delete before header set |
| 2026-11-13_egress-header-replacement (#6608) | #6607 | draft headers committed only on plugin success |
| 2026-11-13_session-gc-companion-index (#6611) | #6609 | reversed-string binary-search companion lookup |
| 2026-11-13_lazy-messages-by-id (#6612) | #6610 | messagesById built only when needed |
| 2026-11-13_session-identity-query (#6615) | #6613 | point SELECT for session removal identity |
| 2026-11-13_block-content-join (#6618) | #6616 | block content materialized only for requested ids |
| 2026-11-13_loop-multiline-sse (#6619) | #6614 | shared sseEventData/replaceSseEventData across adapters |
| 2026-11-13_cleanup-accounting (#6622) | #6620 | cleanup accounting |
| 2026-11-13_gemini-complete-frame (#6623) | #6621 | one wire frame per chunk, non-call parts kept |
| 2026-11-13_count-active-blocks (#6626) | #6624 | SQL COUNT(*) instead of full block decode |
| 2026-11-13_commandcode-proxy-tools (#6627) | #6625 | ACP tool receipts hidden from CommandCode wire |
| 2026-11-13_loop-stream-cleanup (#6630) | #6628 | cancel upstream on in-band parse error + compress finally |
| 2026-11-13_google-stream-errors (#6631) | #6629 | in-band google error frames become terminal events |

## Verification

- All 40 branches reviewed line-by-line before batching (all kept, all with hermetic `node:test` coverage).
- Per-PR added-line audit: every line added by each PR is present in this branch (40/40 clean).
- `tsc --noEmit`: clean.
- All 40 added test suites + the #5403/#5418 watermark suite, run locally on node 22.23.4 with the exact CI preload set: 376/376 pass.

Closes #6483 #6486 #6488 #6490 #6493 #6495 #6497 #6499 #6501 #6503 #6555 #6558 #6562 #6565 #6570 #6573 #6576 #6578 #6580 #6582 #6584 #6590 #6594 #6596 #6598 #6600 #6601 #6605 #6607 #6609 #6610 #6613 #6616 #6614 #6620 #6621 #6624 #6625 #6628 #6629

pr.title: [PR] fix: retain reconciliation brackets for very long histories
pr.author: Afloat16
pr.body:
Closes #6490

## Problem

A long session can fail reconciliation even when almost all re-minted message IDs have verified positional matches. The gap-resolution pass expands every claimed index into Math.min/Math.max arguments; 150,000 claims exceed the JavaScript engine's argument limit and throw RangeError before the folded history is reconciled.

## Change

Maintain the smallest and largest verified indices as the head and tail scans claim positions. This removes both the unbounded argument list and the temporary claimed-index array. Existing fingerprint, role, length, content and no-evidence rules are unchanged; an unbracketed gap remains unmatched.

## Initial validation

- Independent base: 9674cfafbc78c50245ae0d887483d3d6ce880c15.
- Unmodified source: the new 150,001-message regression fails with RangeError at Math.min(...claimedIdx); three controls pass.
- Fixed source: 117 tests pass across fold-reconcile-large-history, fold-reconcile, issue2915-order-centric-reconcile, fold-reconcile-positional and fold-reconcile-perf.
- The new cases exercise a verified middle gap, gaps outside both ends of a bracket, no verified claims, and a 150,001-message unchanged-history fast path. Existing cases cover resync, tail/head shifts, re-keying and evidence gates.
- npm run typecheck, npm run build, npm run check:unused-exports, npm run check:test-import-graph and git diff --check pass.
- Tests run on Linux x64 / Node 24.22.1. Zero-token Codex preflight finds codex-cli 0.167.0-alpha.4 and the built artifact; its local upstream /models probe is unreachable. The real-model suite remains gated/skipped, and full upstream CI was not verified by these initial local checks.

## Prior work and tracking

Checked all 61 Afloat16 PRs, all 160 fork branches, the full fold-reconcile history and upstream issue/PR searches for claimedIdx, reconciliation/argument limits and call-stack failures. #6246 fixes plugin-render's fold-anchor placement, a separate endpoint; it does not cover this reconciliation pass.

## Earlier master integration

Merged upstream master `fcc2e848486cc2152e36b6658c517fbfa51ec428` into this branch without textual conflicts. pr.title: [PR] fix: honor Request cancellation in the inline engine
pr.author: Afloat16
pr.body:
Closes #6503

## Problem

Inline dispatch accepts a Request object but observes only init.signal. A caller using new Request(url, { signal }) can cancel before response headers or during streaming, yet the inline engine continues forwarding work and the caller's body read remains pending. A pre-aborted Request is also sent upstream.

## Changes

Resolve the effective signal from Request when init.signal is omitted or undefined. Preserve explicit replacement signals and null overrides. Check cancellation before and after request conversion, then reuse the existing pre-header rejection and post-header stream/transport cancellation path.

## Original feature validation

On unchanged master 9674cfafbc78c50245ae0d887483d3d6ce880c15, the new real loopback HTTP suite reports 4 failing regressions and 2 passing override controls. It covers omitted init, undefined init.signal, a committed streaming body, and a pre-aborted Request. Cancellation tests verify the actual upstream connection closes; pre-header errors retain the caller's exact reason.

After completing the build, all 14 tests across inline-request-signal, inline-streaming and pi-inline pass, including existing POST model dispatch, init.signal cancellation, live token delivery and admin/transport integration.

Passed: npm run typecheck; npm run build; npm run check:unused-exports; npm run check:test-import-graph; git diff --check.

The zero-token Codex preflight finds the CLI/distribution but its local model endpoint is unreachable; its real-model case is skipped. Full real-model E2E and upstream CI remain unverified. Request body conversion keeps the existing eager-buffering behavior; this change does not make a pending request-body read interruptible.

## Prior work and submission

Checked 61 author PRs, 166 fork heads, complete inline-engine history, and Request.signal/inline/abort PR and issue searches. The cancellation introduced with #3284 observes init.signal only; no prior change was found for inheritance from a Request.

## Current master integration

Merged upstream `fcc2e848486cc2152e36b6658c517fbfa51ec428` into this branch without rewriting the existing feature commit. Integration head: `1c6d2c5cee73c3bd951c224be4a342098a291e7f`. The merge parents are the original feature head `9bcd9c44488c9225da46e57e86eb81f49f9beddc` and the upstream commit above.

The production file and feature test are byte-for-byte unchanged from the original feature head. Relative to current master, this PR still changes only `src/inline-engine.ts` and `tests/inline-request-signal.test.ts`.

Revalidated the merged tree on Node 24.22.1:

- All 14 tests across `inline-request-signal`, `inline-streaming`, and `pi-inline` pass, using the repository's storage and test-environment preloads.
- `npm run typecheck`, `npm run build`, `npm run check:unused-exports`, and `npm run check:test-import-graph` pass.
- `git diff fcc2e848486cc2152e36b6658c517fbfa51ec428 --check` is clean for this PR's net changes.

The original failure/control reproduction above remains tied to `9674cfafbc78c50245ae0d887483d3d6ce880c15`; the validation in this section was rerun after integrating current master. The dispatch and cancellation cases use loopback HTTP fixtures, and full real-model E2E was not rerun locally. Request-body conversion retains its existing eager buffering and does not make an in-progress body read interruptible.

## Review status

Linked to #6503 and ready for maintainer review. The branch now includes current master and is mergeable; GitHub no longer reports it as behind. [CI run 43377731925](https://github.com/ranxianglei/billion-context/actions/runs/43377731925) was queued for this exact integration head when this update was prepared. The [Checks tab](https://github.com/ranxianglei/billion-context/pull/6504/checks) contains the current hosted results.

Please apply the existing `ci:full` label to run the FULL matrix, including the required Windows / Node 24 checks. The default CORE matrix does not produce those checks.

final_integration.title: [PR] chore(branch): land 14 single-purpose fixes as one history-preserving batch (waves 7+8)
final_integration.author: ranxianglei
final_integration.body:
Supersedes #6723 and #6755 (which was accidentally merged into the batch7-wave7 branch instead of master). Head contains both waves: 14 of Afloat16's single-purpose fixes, each merged in with a real merge commit so every original commit and author is preserved in the first-parent history.

Wave 7:

| #6716 | 2026-11-14_linear-coverage-timestamps | #6715 | compression-receipt coverage times: the covered-id dedupe scanned the array per id (`covered.some`, O(n²) on stamped 20k-message folds) → Map, boundary-ref resolution and "never invent a range" semantics unchanged |
| #6718 | 2026-11-14_frozen-message-whitespace | #6717 | frozen-snapshot message re-parse stripped ALL trailing blank lines from every body (content at the end of a message was silently eaten) and lost the ref marker when a body started with a blank line → only the single separator newline before the next header is removed; leading/trailing blanks survive verbatim |
| #6722 | 2026-11-14_linear-cache-usage-alignment | #6721 | cache-diff usage alignment: each usage sample re-scanned every request from the back (O(samples×requests) on 10k-request logs) → single forward pointer over the two sorted lists, same 50 ms admission boundary and stable ordering |

Wave 8:

| #6725 | 2026-11-14_jsonl-historian-null | #6724 | historian JSONL export crashed on a stored content of literal JSON `null` (`message.text` on a non-object) → non-object rows now stay verbatim in full exports |
| #6727 | 2026-11-14_jsonl-ccr-originals | #6726 | full JSONL export dereferenced CCR placeholders to the indexed ENTRY metadata instead of the stored original bytes → resolve byRef→byHash, disk store fills gaps, corrupt/missing mirror keeps the placeholder |
| #6733 | 2026-11-14_join-message-content | #6732 | message readers decoded content with one content-store lookup PER ROW → metadata query stays separate, bodies fetched in bounded 500-row batches (sqlite JOIN for pointer reads, same on the mysql backend) |
| #6735 | 2026-11-14_keepalive-body-failures | #6734 | keepalive pings swallowed every `resp.text()` error (a 200 with a truncated/gzip-mangled body was treated as a normal miss) → body read errors now use the fail-streak budget, 429 keeps first-response disarming, an old response cannot spend the replacement snapshot's budget |
| #6739 | 2026-11-14_keepalive-rotated-timers | #6737 | credential rotation deleted the registry entry but never cancelled the scheduled ping — the dropped snapshot stayed referenced until its old cadence fired → `disarm(..., "credential-rotated")` |
| #6738 | 2026-11-14_cache-diff-insertion-boundaries | #6736 | cache-diff "mid-insert append" misclassified inserting a WHOLE message between existing ones as a semantic append (byte shape is identical) → require same element count with exactly one span growing by the insertion; growth before the root array now reports preArray divergence |
| #6742 | 2026-11-14_usage-log-attribution-tags | #6740 | usage-log parsing attributed samples to the new logger's `[v=]`/`[sess=]` tags (or a request scope) instead of the explicit session → strip logger tags, require the session tag directly before `[acp-usage]`, never invent one |
| #6743 | 2026-11-14_nested-upstream-error-codes | #6741 | upstream alert errno extraction only read the outer `error.code` — native fetch failures nest the errno in `cause` → walk the cause chain (depth-capped, cycle-safe), outer nonempty code keeps precedence |
| #6747 | 2026-11-14_linear-fold-registration | #6744 | batch fold registration re-scanned the whole fold list to close open records per block (O(folds×blocks)) → closeFrom cursor; batch/individual parity kept |
| #6748 | 2026-11-14_linear-handoff-capture | #6746 | handoff reply metering re-encapsulated the entire accumulated text on every delta (O(n²)) → incremental byte accounting with surrogate-pair junction correction; exact UTF-8 budget boundaries kept |
| #6750 | 2026-11-14_diagnostics-unicode-bounds | #6749 | diagnostics truncation used plain `slice`, which can split a surrogate pair at the bound → `safePrefix` everywhere the bound applies (log tails, config, conflict detail, topic) |

Verification: as reported in #6723 and #6755 (per-PR added-line audits clean, tsc clean, 297 test assertions passing across all 14 touched test files on node 22.23.4 with the CI preload chain).

After this merges, the 14 source PRs become branch ancestors of master and close with their Closes keywords.

Closes #6715 #6717 #6721 #6724 #6726 #6732 #6734 #6736 #6737 #6740 #6741 #6744 #6746 #6749

test: fix generatedAt 1ms flake in cache-fold batch/individual parity test

buildSessionCacheReport stamps generatedAt: Date.now() at build time. The
batch/individual parity test deepEqual'd two reports built 1ms apart, so it
flaked whenever the two builds straddled a millisecond boundary (CI red on
ubuntu 22/1 and windows 22/4: generatedAt ...904 vs ...905). Normalize
generatedAt to 0 before the comparison — it is a generation-time marker, not
part of the ledger/report parity being asserted. All ledger data already
matched; only the wall-clock field differed.

head_revalidation.message:
Ask OpenCode for its models once more when its plugins are still starting (R2.2) (#1882)

OpenCode's private server can answer the model check with a 503 ServiceUnavailableError while its plugins start, which stopped a question or build before it began. The check now asks once more after a two-second pause when that typed answer is what it got. Any other failure, a timeout or a stop isn't retried, and a second 503 is the error as before. For #1859.

head_revalidation.subject: docs(serve): settle the PR watch design's status and answered questions (#17250)
head_revalidation.message:
docs(serve): settle the PR watch design's status and answered questions (#17250)

* docs(serve): settle the PR watch design's status and answered questions

The master design still read as a proposal after both of its increments
landed, and two of its open questions had been answered by the maintainer
without the document being told. A reader could not tell which parts were
history and which were still ahead.

Records the landed status while keeping the PR A / PR B sequencing as the
historical record, moves the default and the CI predicate into a settled list
with the channel's opposing rationale preserved rather than dismissed, and
renumbers the questions that remain — the self-push section pointed at a
question number that no longer exists.

Two rows of the affected-files table also contradicted the corrected migration
section: one still described an internal switch that was removed rather than
flipped, the other still said to remove the watch pass that the section now
says to split. Both are aligned, and the remaining open questions keep their
own numbering.

* docs(serve): carry the settled status through the sibling PR watch designs

Review found three gaps in the first commit, and auditing it found a fourth
that the review had not reached.

The migration section still said PR B turns the internal switch on while the
repaired table row said it was removed, so the document contradicted itself
ten lines apart. The increment design the status line now points at still
called itself a proposal and described the switch as still off. And the
renumbering broke twelve inbound citations across eight sibling files, which
were correct before this change and are wrong because of it.

Those citations now name the questions instead of numbering them, so the next
renumbering cannot break them again. The inherited-question lists drop the two
settled items and record when they were settled.

The three PR A designs also still called themselves proposals, and the
enablement design still said PR B turns the switch on — the same contradiction
one document over, introduced by repairing the master. Their status lines now
name the PRs that landed them. Their as-designed goal and scope statements are
left intact, with a note saying the body describes the increment as designed,
because rewriting a design record into the present tense would destroy what
makes it useful.

Every repaired claim has an A/B cell against the shipped tree and a positive
control that reddens the named assertion: 54 cells flip, 28 of 28 controls
killed, seven code oracles true, all ten files restored byte-identical.

* docs(serve): point the Chinese sibling designs at their own language

The previous commit claimed body links point at their own language, but the
check behind that claim only covered four of the ten files. Five links in the
three Chinese PR A designs still pointed at English targets, all on the status
lines this PR had just rewritten — the same defect class it fixed in the
increment design, missed because the gate's scope was narrower than the claim.

The gate now covers all ten files, and the claim is measured across forty links
rather than asserted.

The drain design also lacked the note its two siblings carry, so its body still
read as current mechanism while describing a switch that no longer exists. It
now says the body describes the increment as designed, in both languages,
matching the observation design's wording.

Thirty-two positive controls, each reverting one claim and requiring the named
assertion to redden; all killed, every tree restored byte-identical.

* docs(serve): name the mechanism and the keys the code actually has

Three more verified findings, all the same class as the ones before: a
statement about the removed switch, or about the surface it deprecated, that
the earlier sweeps did not reach.

The drain status line ended the production-inert period at the deps increment,
but the switch stayed false after it, so the period actually ended when PR B
removed the switch — and the opening contradicted the decision five lines below
it, which this PR had already corrected. The validation plan still asked for a
test of a constant that no longer exists; it now asks for the effect, which is
what the shipped tests pin. And the migration section named two of the four keys
connect() deprecates, so an implementer following it would leave two knobs with
no rejection path while the warning called them deprecated.

Auditing that last fix found the same two-of-four gap in the increment design's
own deprecation section, one document over. Both now name all four, in both
languages, matching what the adapter's predicate and its single warning do.

Sixty-seven A/B cells flip against the shipped tree with none regressing, seven
code oracles hold, and forty-two positive controls each redden the assertion
they name. Every tree restored byte-identical.

* docs(serve): stop the validation plan from asking for what the code does not do

Auditing the previous repair found three more claims in the master design that
the shipped adapter contradicts, all in the sections a reader would use to
decide what to test.

The validation plan asked for the watch state file to be "read once and
renamed". The retirement strips the file in place and never renames it — the
comment cursors live in it, and the same document's migration section already
says so. The criterion now asks for the strip, which is what the adapter test
observes when it reads the file back at its original path.

The plan and acceptance criterion 3 both said the channel "runs no watch pass".
The pass still runs: it carries the comment watch, which is on by default. What
is gone is the state detection inside it. Saying otherwise is the same mistake
the affected-files row made before this PR repaired it, and it would send a
reader to delete a pass that comment delivery depends on.

The channel row's deprecation clause named two of the four keys, one paragraph
after the migration section was corrected to name all four. It now names four,
with the alias scoped to the two surfaces that actually produce one.

Two new code oracles back these: the retirement body saves the state file and
contains no rename, and the pass still has a call site behind the comment gate.
Both were probed for vacuity — a rename inside the body, a removed save, a
missing function and a rename outside the body each flip the first as expected.

Eighty-one A/B cells flip against the shipped tree with none regressing.

* docs(serve): give the enablement design the same as-designed note as its siblings

The observation and drain designs both carry a status-line note saying the body
describes the increment as designed, which is what lets their present-tense
"current state" sections stay useful as a record after the mechanism changed.
The enablement design never got one, and it needs it more than either: its
problem statement says nothing in production populates the drain's deps, which
stopped being true when this very increment landed, not when PR B did.

The note now says what this increment did and what PR B did after it, so a
reader who lands on "no production caller" knows which tree that sentence
describes. Both languages, one clause each, matching the siblings' wording.

Eighty-three A/B cells flip against the shipped tree with none regressing.

* docs(serve): say what PR B removes, and close the four-key scope everywhere

The automatic review on the previous head found the enablement design's
non-goals still saying "Removing the adapter watch: PR B". That is the same
delete-the-pass error this PR repaired in the master's affected-files row, and
it is wrong even as a design record: the split was always the plan, and the
pass still runs today as the comment carrier. The bullet now names what PR B
removes — the adapter's PR-state detection and delivery — and says the pass
stays. The surrounding as-designed voice is kept, with the status-line note
carrying the tense, which is the remedy already accepted for the sibling bodies.

Acceptance criterion 3 ended with "it is rejected at connect()", where "it"
read as the two alias surfaces the criterion opens with, while the migration
section and the increment design both reject four keys. The closing clause now
names all four, so the two paths an implementer might follow agree.

The Chinese migration paragraph opened an em-dash aside for the four keys and
never closed it, which pulled "and drops the alias" inside the enumeration.
Parentheses close it unambiguously.

Eighty-nine A/B cells flip against the shipped tree with none regressing.

* docs(serve): the drain design's problem statement also said PR B deletes the pass

Sweeping the whole family for the phrase the previous commit repaired found one
more site: the drain design's problem statement ends with "the drain stays off
until PR B removes the adapter watch", in both languages. Same error, same
reason — the pass was always going to be split, and it still runs as the comment
carrier. It now says PR B removes the adapter's state detection, which is what
the switchover actually consists of.

The surrounding as-designed voice is unchanged; the status-line note carries the
tense, as it does for the rest of the body.

Ninety-three A/B cells flip against the shipped tree with none regressing.

* docs(serve): widen the window decision, name the real user docs, own the test gap

The review on the previous head found three more, and one of them is a claim
this PR itself made too strongly.

Decision 6 defines the deprecation window, and it still scoped it to the two
aliased keys while the migration section, acceptance criterion 3 and the
increment design all reject four. An implementer following the decision would
leave the documented close unimplemented. The decision now covers all four, keeps
the release-notes rationale for the two surfaces that have one, and says why the
two inert knobs ride the same window: an operator carrying only one of them
should get the warning before the rejection.

The validation plan asked for the unprovisioned-seam effect, and this PR's own
description said the shipped tests pin it. They do not. Both no-deps tests end at
asserting the getter was consulted — one seeds no watch file and asserts no
delivery, the other has no negative assertion on the view call. The plan keeps
the effect as the criterion, because that is the right criterion, and now records
that the assertions are still owed instead of implying they exist. Strengthening
those two tests is a code change and is listed as a follow-up.

The affected-files docs row promised a new sessionPrWatch user page that does not
exist. The setting is documented in the channel feature page and three rows of
the settings reference; the row now names those. A new code oracle pins that: no
dedicated page under docs/users, exactly three settings rows, and the channel page
mentions the setting.

One hundred and three A/B cells flip against the shipped tree with none
regressing.

* docs(serve): reconcile the status line, the CI predicate, and two terms

The review on the previous head found five, and two of them are contradictions
this PR's own earlier fixes introduced.

The status line said the one piece still ahead is the deprecation close, while
the validation plan two screens below records two effect assertions as owed. Both
sentences are this PR's; the status line now lists both, so a maintainer reading
it as the completion record does not close the tracker with the negative path
unasserted.

The Chinese inherited-question bullets named the master design 母设计 in two files
that define and otherwise use 主设计 — a term those documents never introduce.
Both now use their own term. The increment design keeps 母设计 throughout, which is
its own established usage.

Decision 5 described the shipped CI predicate as reading rollup.state. It does
not: aggregateChecks walks the rollup entries and reads each entry's own state or
conclusion. The decision now says that, so the next increment that tries to
suppress cancelled/stale noise designs against the mechanism that exists. A new
oracle pins both halves — the loop is there, and no rollup-level state read is.

The increment design's deprecation section said the validation "throws today"
beside a sentence describing the warning that ships today, with a symbol that no
longer exists at head. Its status line already scopes citations to the commit
they were read at, so the sentence now says "threw at that commit" and "became",
which removes the ambiguity about whether the warn path shipped.

The affected-files docs row omitted docs/developers/daemon/17-configuration.md,
which PR B's merge commit also changed; the row is meant to serve as the change
inventory, so it now names all four targets. A second new oracle pins that the
merge commit touched that file.

One hundred and fifteen A/B cells flip against the shipped tree with none
regressing; nine further negative cells are absent in both arms and are not
counted as flips.

* docs(serve): correct the seam's default direction, and finish the family's framing

Three items from the review on the previous head. The first is a factual error
about code that still exists, not historical framing.

The observation design's resolved-implementation bullet said the test seam
defaults to the removed constant and that production omits it, so the constant
governs. The seam is still declared, and its documented semantics are the
opposite: false forces the watch off, absent or true leaves enablement to deps
presence. A test author reading the design would get the fallback backwards. The
bullet now describes the shipped mechanism and keeps the seam, with a new oracle
pinning the comment and both gates.

The increment design had its status flipped to implemented and its line numbers
scoped to the commit they were read at, but not its body — while the three sibling
designs each got an explicit as-designed sentence in this same change. Its current
state section still says the cap is three mechanisms and the drain's config seams
are dead, both false at head. It now carries the same sentence, so a reader can
tell which statements describe that commit and which describe today.

The three increment statuses used "landed", a status value new to docs/design:
172 files lead with "implemented" and an inventory grepping for that value would
silently miss these three. All five documents now use one status value, keeping
the landing PR numbers as detail.

One hundred and twenty-one A/B cells flip against the shipped tree with none
regressing; eleven further negative cells are absent in both arms.

* docs(serve): finish the de-numbering, the per-entry predicate, and §7's tense

Three items from the review on the previous head. Two of them are gaps between
what this change claims to do and what it had actually done, which is why they are
fixed here rather than deferred.

The description says the inbound question citations now name the questions rather
than numbering them, so a future renumbering cannot break them again. One was
still numbered: the self-push bullet's "(still-open question 3)", renumbered in an
earlier pass instead of de-numbered like the other twelve. It now names the
manual-push ledger question. A family-wide sweep confirms no numbered question
citation remains in any of the ten files, and a ledger cell asserts that over all
ten rather than at the flagged site.

Decision 8 of the increment design still described the CI predicate as reading
rollup-level rollup.state — the same mechanism error repaired one document over in
master decision 5. A reader following decision 5's pointer for the reasoning would
carry away a model of a field that does not exist. It now says enumerating contexts
and special-casing those conclusions, versus reading each entry's own state or
conclusion, matching the master. The sweep shows rollup.state is gone from all ten
files, pinned by a cell over the whole family.

§7's PR A paragraph was past tense while the adjacent PR B paragraph still narrated
pending work, so the two disagreed about landedness under a status line that says
PR B landed. The verbs that narrate the change are now past in both languages; the
descriptions of shipped behaviour stay present, and the sequencing is kept as the
historical record the status line declares.

One hundred and twenty-nine A/B cells flip against the shipped tree with none
regressing.

* docs(serve): scope the alias promise to two keys, and cite the knobs' validation

The requested high-effort review returned four Suggestions and no Criticals. Two
are inside this change's ten files and one of those is a regression this change
introduced, so they are fixed here; the other two need files outside the declared
set and are recorded as follow-ups in the PR thread.

Decision 6's headline read "One-release deprecation window with aliases for all
four deprecated keys" after the window was widened to four. Only two of the four
are aliased — the same decision's body says "the first two are read as aliases",
the migration section calls the knobs now-inert, and the shipped warning says they
are ignored. A maintainer planning the close from the key-decisions list would
implement alias handling for a knob that should be dropped as inert. The headline
now names the window, and the alias promise is scoped to the first two explicitly.

The deprecation section's citation covered only the two event keys. At the commit
it cites, the knobs were rejected in validateBoundSessionConfig, outside every
span the sentence named, and normalizePrWatchEvents contains neither — so an
implementer restoring the rejection would find nothing to restore for the knobs.
The citation now names both functions and the three knob spans. A new oracle pins
that split at the cited commit: the event-key function contains neither knob, and
the config validator contains both.

One hundred and thirty-three A/B cells flip against the shipped tree with none
regressing.

head_revalidation.subject: fix(chunking): don't emit a chunk that holds only the overlap when overlap_all splits an element (#4598)
head_revalidation.message:
fix(chunking): don't emit a chunk that holds only the overlap when overlap_all splits an element (#4598)

## Summary

With `overlap=N` and `overlap_all=True`, chunking can emit a chunk that
holds
only the last N characters of the previous chunk, and the chunk after it
starts by repeating most of that tail. This happens in
`chunk_elements()`,
`chunk_by_title()` and `partition(..., chunking_strategy=...,
overlap_all=True)`
when an element does not fit next to the overlap prefix (the normal case
for
an element longer than `max_characters`) and the prefix is a full N
characters long, that is, the last N characters of the previous chunk do
not
start with whitespace.

Example (`max_characters=50, overlap=10, overlap_all=True`):

```python
chunk_elements(
    [
        Text("Lorem ipsum dolor sit amet, consectetur."),
        Text("In rhoncus ipsum sed lectus porta volutpat, ut aliquet magna."),
    ],
    max_characters=50, overlap=10, overlap_all=True,
)
```

- On `main`: `"Lorem ipsum dolor sit amet, consectetur."`,
`"nsectetur."`,
  `"sectetur. In rhoncus ipsum sed lectus porta"`,
  `"tus porta volutpat, ut aliquet magna."`
- With this PR: `"Lorem ipsum dolor sit amet, consectetur."`,
  `"nsectetur.\n\nIn rhoncus ipsum sed lectus porta"`,
  `"tus porta volutpat, ut aliquet magna."`

A repository fixture shows it too:
`partition_text("example-docs/book-war-and-peace-1p.txt",
chunking_strategy="by_title", max_characters=300, overlap=40,
overlap_all=True)`
gives two chunks that are only the 40-character overlap:
`'you--sit down and tell me all the news."'` and
`'ight between 7 and 10--Annette Scherer."'`.

Cause: `overlap_all` joins the overlap prefix to the next element with a
blank line (`"\n\n"`). When the result is too long, `_TextSplitter`
splits it
with `_split_from_maxlen()`. That function starts its separator search
at
`overlap + 1` so that the split comes out longer than the overlap (its
comment: "A split not longer than overlap will not progress"). But the
search
can match the second `"\n"` of the blank line.
`s[:match_start].rstrip()`
then strips the first `"\n"`, so the fragment is exactly the prefix
(length == overlap).

Fix, in `unstructured/chunking/base.py`: after the fragment is trimmed,
`_split_from_maxlen()` returns `"", s` when `len(fragment) <= overlap`.
The
splitter then falls back to the next separator (`" "`), and the prefix
shares
a chunk with the start of the element. This mirrors the existing guard
on the
token-counting path in `_split_by_tokens()`
(`overlap == 0 or fragment_tokens > overlap`). The fixed output has the
same
shape as the one `main` already gives when the prefix is shorter than
`overlap`: with `overlap=13` the example's stripped prefix is
`"consectetur."` (12 characters), and chunk 2 on `main` is
`"consectetur.\n\nIn rhoncus ipsum sed lectus porta"`.

Related: open PR #4392 also changes overlap splitting, but only
`_split_by_tokens()` (an infinite loop in token-based overlap). This PR
changes
only the character path (`_split_from_maxlen()` is called only from the
character branch of `_TextSplitter.__call__`), so the two do not
overlap.

## Validation

Environment: worktree on `upstream/main` (c74e6c4), Python 3.12.3,
`uv sync --locked --group test --extra docx --extra chunking-tokens`.

New tests:

-
`test_unstructured/chunking/test_base.py::Describe_TextSplitter::but_it_does_not_split_off_a_fragment_no_longer_than_the_overlap`
splits `"nsectetur.\n\nIn rhoncus ipsum sed lectus porta volutpat, ut
aliquet magna."`
  with `max_characters=50, overlap=10`.
-
`test_unstructured/chunking/test_basic.py::test_it_does_not_emit_a_chunk_holding_only_the_overlap_when_overlap_all_splits_an_element`
  runs the `chunk_elements()` example above.

Results:

- New tests without the fix:
`pytest
"test_unstructured/chunking/test_base.py::Describe_TextSplitter::but_it_does_not_split_off_a_fragment_no_longer_than_the_overlap"
"test_unstructured/chunking/test_basic.py::test_it_does_not_emit_a_chunk_holding_only_the_overlap_when_overlap_all_splits_an_element"`
gives 2 failed. The unit test gets `s == "nsectetur."` (only the
overlap).
The integration test gets `"nsectetur."` as chunk 2 plus one extra
chunk.
- New tests with the fix: 2 passed.
`pytest test_unstructured/chunking/test_base.py::Describe_TextSplitter`:
  9 passed.
- `pytest test_unstructured/chunking/test_basic.py`: 23 passed.
- `pytest test_unstructured/chunking/test_base.py`: 334 passed, 16
skipped,
55 failed. All 55 failures are token-mode tests: `tiktoken` cannot
download
`cl100k_base` from `openaipublic.blob.core.windows.net` in my
environment
  (proxy 403). They do not reach the changed function.
- `pytest test_unstructured/chunking/`: without the fix (new tests
included)
  65 failed, 607 passed, 18 skipped. With the fix 63 failed, 609 passed,
18 skipped. The two failure sets differ only by the 2 new tests. Each of
the
  63 remaining failures has "token" in its test id and fails on the
  `tiktoken` download above.
- War and Peace fixture call above: 19 chunks before, with 2
overlap-only
chunks. 17 chunks after, none overlap-only, longest chunk 300
characters.
- Randomized check, 3000 `chunk_elements()` runs (`max_characters`
30-300,
  `overlap` up to `max_characters // 2`, mixed `NarrativeText` and
`CodeSnippet`, `overlap_all=True` in about 70% of runs). Before: 4166
chunks
that are a suffix of the previous chunk, no longer than `overlap`, and
not an
input element's text. After: 0. No chunk is longer than `max_characters`
in
  either run, and every run terminates.
- `make check` (ruff 0.15.10 from the `lint` group): `All checks
passed!`,
  `355 files already formatted`.
- `bash scripts/test-check-new-release-version.sh`: `Passed 27 version
guard tests.`
- `VERSION_BASE_REF=upstream/main bash
scripts/check-new-release-version.sh`:
  `PASS: unchanged development version 0.27.35-dev (no tag lookup).`
- No `CHANGELOG.md` or `unstructured/__version__.py` changes.

## Release note

With `overlap_all=True`, chunking no longer emits a chunk that contains
only
the overlap copied from the previous chunk when it splits a long
element. The
overlap now shares a chunk with the start of that element, so documents
chunked this way can produce fewer chunks than before.

## Checklist

conventional commit prefix.
- [ ] Apply a category label (`enhancement`, `bug`, or an appropriate
existing label), or ask a maintainer to apply it. A maintainer needs to
apply `bug`.
- [ ] For breaking changes, use `!` in the title and explain impact and
migration above. (Not a breaking change.)

head_revalidation.subject: SfM: Update visibility on feature transitions (CPU perf) (#5006)
head_revalidation.message:
SfM: Update visibility on feature transitions (CPU perf) (#5006)

## Summary

Update the visibility pyramid only when an image feature gains its first
triangulated correspondence or loses its last. Extra supporting
correspondences leave occupied cells unchanged, so repeating every
pyramid-level update does unnecessary work.

This is a small inherited optimization, based directly on official
COLMAP 3c1a1b957cc96d88849e4d30e1d0ec51c9da501b.

## Changes

- Move SetPoint/ResetPoint into the existing zero/one visibility
transitions.
- Extend the maintained score test with repeated support, distinct
colliding features, partial/final removal and underflow checks.
- Extend AddImage with observation removal and reconstruction of the
manager, avoiding unrelated fork registration behavior.

## Background

The update pattern dates to fe8f82aee9829c6c828158da2695e2d87a977f74,
"Initial commit" (2016), in src/base/image.cc. It was retained by
eaebe3c34b535e38d9101a5eba81cde994b9b279, "Add ObservationManager
(#2575)".

## Results

The source-equivalent transition change was measured in a composed-fork
fixed bookkeeping probe: Add64/Delete32/Delete32 on 16 images, 64 tracks
and 120 pairs.

| Platform | Before | After |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Linux/WSL | 1.395 ms | 0.640 ms |
| Windows | 2.776 ms | 1.438 ms |

Each table value is the arithmetic mean of four fresh process means per
arm (ABBAABBA). Each process mean averages ten measured batches after
two warmups. Canonical inputs and outputs agree within each platform.
These are fixed bookkeeping timings, not reconstruction throughput
measurements.

## Validation

- Independent source review accepted the clean-base production change
and adapted lifecycle fixture.
- Clean base and candidate each passed all 15 maintained manager cases,
without skips.
- Configured clang-tidy-18 checked observation_manager.cc in both arms
and the maintained test with no displayed source diagnostics;
generated/header warnings were suppressed.
- Reused retained pristine-upstream support and rebuilt the two selected
consumers of newer RANSAC headers; final source, link and provider
checks passed.
- Separately, the composed-fork version passed 18 manager and two mapper
cases on Linux and Windows.

head_revalidation.message:
feat(web): navigate the chat transcript from the keyboard (#1382)

* feat(web): navigate the chat transcript from the keyboard

The transcript is one Tab stop: a feed of articles (rows plus the steps of an expanded activity or thinking group) built from data, so moves reach rows Virtuoso has unmounted. Arrows and hjkl move and expand, C copies, O opens a tool's file, Shift+F10 opens an item menu, Esc returns to the composer, and Tab walks the focused item's own controls. Ctrl/Cmd+Up enters from the composer and PgUp/PgDn scroll from it; keyboard Latest and a history jump focus what they reveal, Stop refocuses the composer. History entries take Delete and Shift+F10, the covered transcript is inert under Resources, a composer popup takes Escape first, and hjkl repeat the arrows on tab strips and rails.

* fix(web): reveal a nested step of the newest transcript group instead of jumping to the latest edge

* fix(ui): count a details element's summary as tabbable

head_revalidation.subject: Stop message capture from dropping attributes without a trace (#437)
head_revalidation.message:
Stop message capture from dropping attributes without a trace (#437)

* Stop message capture from dropping attributes without a trace

Two cases made gen_ai.input.messages / gen_ai.output.messages vanish
from chat attempt spans with capture_messages on:

- Tool-call arguments that are not valid JSON (a truncated answer, or
  one containing NaN or Infinity) raised while the messages were built,
  so the rejected answer was missing from its own attempt span and the
  request was missing from the re-ask span that replays it. The raw
  argument string is now kept.
- A serialized attribute over max_attribute_length was skipped with
  nothing left behind. Its size is now recorded as
  <key>.original_length, the companion attribute truncated payloads
  already use.

Both were reported from a consumer probe of the 2.16.0 pre-release
head. The new tests fail on the previous code, including three that
drive a real Instructor client over a mock transport. Core suite:
1373 passed, 14 skipped; message_payloads.py is at 100% coverage.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5.2 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Describe the message capture fallbacks in the release notes and map

The 2.16.0 notes and the codebase map now say that an oversized
messages attribute leaves its size in <key>.original_length and that
unparseable tool-call arguments are kept as raw text.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5.2 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commit_count_note: Merged author PRs, account-linked default-branch author commits and official Contributors-graph commits are independently measured. Author inventories include author-created merge commits; graph counts exclude merges and empty commits. Billion-context currently has 193 author entries including 45 author-created merges, leaving 148 non-merge graph commits. Agentes Chat has two author entries, including one author-created merge commit; its graph shows the remaining non-merge commit. Indirect maintainer adoption does not increase the direct merged-author-PR total.
ranking_methodology: All current homepage ranks use the official GitHub Contributors graph: All / Commits / default branch, excluding merge and empty commits under GitHub's documented graph definition. Each page's graphDataPath and current frontend source were read; full weekly data was processed using the exact current comparator, top-100 and ordinal-place logic. Contribution Insights modes omit line counts but retain the same commit ranking. No REST contributor ordering is substituted. Absence from a complete top100 is represented as a dash, not an exact rank or zero contributions. Graph data may be cached.

final_integration.title: [PR] chore(branch): land 14 single-purpose fixes as one history-preserving batch (waves 7+8)
final_integration.author: ranxianglei
final_integration.body:
Supersedes #6723 and #6755 (which was accidentally merged into the batch7-wave7 branch instead of master). Head contains both waves: 14 of Afloat16's single-purpose fixes, each merged in with a real merge commit so every original commit and author is preserved in the first-parent history.

Wave 7:

| #6716 | 2026-11-14_linear-coverage-timestamps | #6715 | compression-receipt coverage times: the covered-id dedupe scanned the array per id (`covered.some`, O(n²) on stamped 20k-message folds) → Map, boundary-ref resolution and "never invent a range" semantics unchanged |
| #6718 | 2026-11-14_frozen-message-whitespace | #6717 | frozen-snapshot message re-parse stripped ALL trailing blank lines from every body (content at the end of a message was silently eaten) and lost the ref marker when a body started with a blank line → only the single separator newline before the next header is removed; leading/trailing blanks survive verbatim |
| #6722 | 2026-11-14_linear-cache-usage-alignment | #6721 | cache-diff usage alignment: each usage sample re-scanned every request from the back (O(samples×requests) on 10k-request logs) → single forward pointer over the two sorted lists, same 50 ms admission boundary and stable ordering |

Wave 8:

| #6725 | 2026-11-14_jsonl-historian-null | #6724 | historian JSONL export crashed on a stored content of literal JSON `null` (`message.text` on a non-object) → non-object rows now stay verbatim in full exports |
| #6727 | 2026-11-14_jsonl-ccr-originals | #6726 | full JSONL export dereferenced CCR placeholders to the indexed ENTRY metadata instead of the stored original bytes → resolve byRef→byHash, disk store fills gaps, corrupt/missing mirror keeps the placeholder |
| #6733 | 2026-11-14_join-message-content | #6732 | message readers decoded content with one content-store lookup PER ROW → metadata query stays separate, bodies fetched in bounded 500-row batches (sqlite JOIN for pointer reads, same on the mysql backend) |
| #6735 | 2026-11-14_keepalive-body-failures | #6734 | keepalive pings swallowed every `resp.text()` error (a 200 with a truncated/gzip-mangled body was treated as a normal miss) → body read errors now use the fail-streak budget, 429 keeps first-response disarming, an old response cannot spend the replacement snapshot's budget |
| #6739 | 2026-11-14_keepalive-rotated-timers | #6737 | credential rotation deleted the registry entry but never cancelled the scheduled ping — the dropped snapshot stayed referenced until its old cadence fired → `disarm(..., "credential-rotated")` |
| #6738 | 2026-11-14_cache-diff-insertion-boundaries | #6736 | cache-diff "mid-insert append" misclassified inserting a WHOLE message between existing ones as a semantic append (byte shape is identical) → require same element count with exactly one span growing by the insertion; growth before the root array now reports preArray divergence |
| #6742 | 2026-11-14_usage-log-attribution-tags | #6740 | usage-log parsing attributed samples to the new logger's `[v=]`/`[sess=]` tags (or a request scope) instead of the explicit session → strip logger tags, require the session tag directly before `[acp-usage]`, never invent one |
| #6743 | 2026-11-14_nested-upstream-error-codes | #6741 | upstream alert errno extraction only read the outer `error.code` — native fetch failures nest the errno in `cause` → walk the cause chain (depth-capped, cycle-safe), outer nonempty code keeps precedence |
| #6747 | 2026-11-14_linear-fold-registration | #6744 | batch fold registration re-scanned the whole fold list to close open records per block (O(folds×blocks)) → closeFrom cursor; batch/individual parity kept |
| #6748 | 2026-11-14_linear-handoff-capture | #6746 | handoff reply metering re-encapsulated the entire accumulated text on every delta (O(n²)) → incremental byte accounting with surrogate-pair junction correction; exact UTF-8 budget boundaries kept |
| #6750 | 2026-11-14_diagnostics-unicode-bounds | #6749 | diagnostics truncation used plain `slice`, which can split a surrogate pair at the bound → `safePrefix` everywhere the bound applies (log tails, config, conflict detail, topic) |

Verification: as reported in #6723 and #6755 (per-PR added-line audits clean, tsc clean, 297 test assertions passing across all 14 touched test files on node 22.23.4 with the CI preload chain).

After this merges, the 14 source PRs become branch ancestors of master and close with their Closes keywords.

Closes #6715 #6717 #6721 #6724 #6726 #6732 #6734 #6736 #6737 #6740 #6741 #6744 #6746 #6749

nested_integration.title: [PR] chore(branch): land 11 single-purpose fixes as one history-preserving batch (wave 8)
nested_integration.author: ranxianglei
nested_integration.body:
Lands Afloat16's 11 latest single-purpose fixes as one history-preserving batch. Each branch is merged in with a real merge commit (`Merge Afloat16/<branch> (PR #<n>) into batch8-wave8`), so every original commit and author is preserved in the first-parent history.

**Base note:** this PR targets `batch7-wave7` (#6723) — #6723 should be merged first, then this one.

| PR | Branch | Issue | What it fixes |
|---|---|---|---|
| #6725 | 2026-11-14_jsonl-historian-null | #6724 | historian JSONL export crashed on a stored content of literal JSON `null` (`message.text` on a non-object) → non-object rows now stay verbatim in full exports |
| #6727 | 2026-11-14_jsonl-ccr-originals | #6726 | full JSONL export dereferenced CCR placeholders to the indexed ENTRY metadata instead of the stored original bytes → resolve byRef→byHash, disk store fills gaps, corrupt/missing mirror keeps the placeholder |
| #6733 | 2026-11-14_join-message-content | #6732 | message readers decoded content with one content-store lookup PER ROW → metadata query stays separate, bodies fetched in bounded 500-row batches (sqlite JOIN for pointer reads, same on the mysql backend) |
| #6735 | 2026-11-14_keepalive-body-failures | #6734 | keepalive pings swallowed every `resp.text()` error (a 200 with a truncated/gzip-mangled body was treated as a normal miss) → body read errors now use the fail-streak budget, 429 keeps first-response disarming, an old response cannot spend the replacement snapshot's budget |
| #6739 | 2026-11-14_keepalive-rotated-timers | #6737 | credential rotation deleted the registry entry but never cancelled the scheduled ping — the dropped snapshot stayed referenced until its old cadence fired → `disarm(..., "credential-rotated")` |
| #6738 | 2026-11-14_cache-diff-insertion-boundaries | #6736 | cache-diff "mid-insert append" misclassified inserting a WHOLE message between existing ones as a semantic append (byte shape is identical) → require same element count with exactly one span growing by the insertion; growth before the root array now reports preArray divergence |
| #6742 | 2026-11-14_usage-log-attribution-tags | #6740 | usage-log parsing attributed samples to the new logger's `[v=]`/`[sess=]` tags (or a request scope) instead of the explicit session → strip logger tags, require the session tag directly before `[acp-usage]`, never invent one |
| #6743 | 2026-11-14_nested-upstream-error-codes | #6741 | upstream alert errno extraction only read the outer `error.code` — native fetch failures nest the errno in `cause` → walk the cause chain (depth-capped, cycle-safe), outer nonempty code keeps precedence |
| #6747 | 2026-11-14_linear-fold-registration | #6744 | batch fold registration re-scanned the whole fold list to close open records per block (O(folds×blocks)) → closeFrom cursor; batch/individual parity kept |
| #6748 | 2026-11-14_linear-handoff-capture | #6746 | handoff reply metering re-encapsulated the entire accumulated text on every delta (O(n²)) → incremental byte accounting with surrogate-pair junction correction; exact UTF-8 budget boundaries kept |
| #6750 | 2026-11-14_diagnostics-unicode-bounds | #6749 | diagnostics truncation used plain `slice`, which can split a surrogate pair at the bound → `safePrefix` everywhere the bound applies (log tails, config, conflict detail, topic) |

Verification (clean checkout of this branch, node 22.23.4, CI preload chain):
- per-PR added-line audit vs its merge-base: all 11 clean
- `tsc --noEmit`: clean
- all 11 touched test files: 187 pass

After this merges, the 11 source PRs become branch ancestors of master and close with their Closes keywords.

Closes #6724 #6726 #6732 #6734 #6736 #6737 #6740 #6741 #6744 #6746 #6749

test: fix generatedAt 1ms flake in cache-fold batch/individual parity test

buildSessionCacheReport stamps generatedAt: Date.now() at build time. The
batch/individual parity test deepEqual'd two reports built 1ms apart, so it
flaked whenever the two builds straddled a millisecond boundary (CI red on
ubuntu 22/1 and windows 22/4: generatedAt ...904 vs ...905). Normalize
generatedAt to 0 before the comparison — it is a generation-time marker, not
part of the ledger/report parity being asserted. All ledger data already
matched; only the wall-clock field differed.

final_integration.title: [PR] chore(branch): land 14 single-purpose fixes as one history-preserving batch (waves 7+8)
final_integration.author: ranxianglei
final_integration.body:
Supersedes #6723 and #6755 (which was accidentally merged into the batch7-wave7 branch instead of master). Head contains both waves: 14 of Afloat16's single-purpose fixes, each merged in with a real merge commit so every original commit and author is preserved in the first-parent history.

Wave 7:

| #6716 | 2026-11-14_linear-coverage-timestamps | #6715 | compression-receipt coverage times: the covered-id dedupe scanned the array per id (`covered.some`, O(n²) on stamped 20k-message folds) → Map, boundary-ref resolution and "never invent a range" semantics unchanged |
| #6718 | 2026-11-14_frozen-message-whitespace | #6717 | frozen-snapshot message re-parse stripped ALL trailing blank lines from every body (content at the end of a message was silently eaten) and lost the ref marker when a body started with a blank line → only the single separator newline before the next header is removed; leading/trailing blanks survive verbatim |
| #6722 | 2026-11-14_linear-cache-usage-alignment | #6721 | cache-diff usage alignment: each usage sample re-scanned every request from the back (O(samples×requests) on 10k-request logs) → single forward pointer over the two sorted lists, same 50 ms admission boundary and stable ordering |

Wave 8:

| #6725 | 2026-11-14_jsonl-historian-null | #6724 | historian JSONL export crashed on a stored content of literal JSON `null` (`message.text` on a non-object) → non-object rows now stay verbatim in full exports |
| #6727 | 2026-11-14_jsonl-ccr-originals | #6726 | full JSONL export dereferenced CCR placeholders to the indexed ENTRY metadata instead of the stored original bytes → resolve byRef→byHash, disk store fills gaps, corrupt/missing mirror keeps the placeholder |
| #6733 | 2026-11-14_join-message-content | #6732 | message readers decoded content with one content-store lookup PER ROW → metadata query stays separate, bodies fetched in bounded 500-row batches (sqlite JOIN for pointer reads, same on the mysql backend) |
| #6735 | 2026-11-14_keepalive-body-failures | #6734 | keepalive pings swallowed every `resp.text()` error (a 200 with a truncated/gzip-mangled body was treated as a normal miss) → body read errors now use the fail-streak budget, 429 keeps first-response disarming, an old response cannot spend the replacement snapshot's budget |
| #6739 | 2026-11-14_keepalive-rotated-timers | #6737 | credential rotation deleted the registry entry but never cancelled the scheduled ping — the dropped snapshot stayed referenced until its old cadence fired → `disarm(..., "credential-rotated")` |
| #6738 | 2026-11-14_cache-diff-insertion-boundaries | #6736 | cache-diff "mid-insert append" misclassified inserting a WHOLE message between existing ones as a semantic append (byte shape is identical) → require same element count with exactly one span growing by the insertion; growth before the root array now reports preArray divergence |
| #6742 | 2026-11-14_usage-log-attribution-tags | #6740 | usage-log parsing attributed samples to the new logger's `[v=]`/`[sess=]` tags (or a request scope) instead of the explicit session → strip logger tags, require the session tag directly before `[acp-usage]`, never invent one |
| #6743 | 2026-11-14_nested-upstream-error-codes | #6741 | upstream alert errno extraction only read the outer `error.code` — native fetch failures nest the errno in `cause` → walk the cause chain (depth-capped, cycle-safe), outer nonempty code keeps precedence |
| #6747 | 2026-11-14_linear-fold-registration | #6744 | batch fold registration re-scanned the whole fold list to close open records per block (O(folds×blocks)) → closeFrom cursor; batch/individual parity kept |
| #6748 | 2026-11-14_linear-handoff-capture | #6746 | handoff reply metering re-encapsulated the entire accumulated text on every delta (O(n²)) → incremental byte accounting with surrogate-pair junction correction; exact UTF-8 budget boundaries kept |
| #6750 | 2026-11-14_diagnostics-unicode-bounds | #6749 | diagnostics truncation used plain `slice`, which can split a surrogate pair at the bound → `safePrefix` everywhere the bound applies (log tails, config, conflict detail, topic) |

Verification: as reported in #6723 and #6755 (per-PR added-line audits clean, tsc clean, 297 test assertions passing across all 14 touched test files on node 22.23.4 with the CI preload chain).

After this merges, the 14 source PRs become branch ancestors of master and close with their Closes keywords.

Closes #6715 #6717 #6721 #6724 #6726 #6732 #6734 #6736 #6737 #6740 #6741 #6744 #6746 #6749

nested_integration.title: [PR] chore(branch): land 11 single-purpose fixes as one history-preserving batch (wave 8)
nested_integration.author: ranxianglei
nested_integration.body:
Lands Afloat16's 11 latest single-purpose fixes as one history-preserving batch. Each branch is merged in with a real merge commit (`Merge Afloat16/<branch> (PR #<n>) into batch8-wave8`), so every original commit and author is preserved in the first-parent history.

**Base note:** this PR targets `batch7-wave7` (#6723) — #6723 should be merged first, then this one.

| PR | Branch | Issue | What it fixes |
|---|---|---|---|
| #6725 | 2026-11-14_jsonl-historian-null | #6724 | historian JSONL export crashed on a stored content of literal JSON `null` (`message.text` on a non-object) → non-object rows now stay verbatim in full exports |
| #6727 | 2026-11-14_jsonl-ccr-originals | #6726 | full JSONL export dereferenced CCR placeholders to the indexed ENTRY metadata instead of the stored original bytes → resolve byRef→byHash, disk store fills gaps, corrupt/missing mirror keeps the placeholder |
| #6733 | 2026-11-14_join-message-content | #6732 | message readers decoded content with one content-store lookup PER ROW → metadata query stays separate, bodies fetched in bounded 500-row batches (sqlite JOIN for pointer reads, same on the mysql backend) |
| #6735 | 2026-11-14_keepalive-body-failures | #6734 | keepalive pings swallowed every `resp.text()` error (a 200 with a truncated/gzip-mangled body was treated as a normal miss) → body read errors now use the fail-streak budget, 429 keeps first-response disarming, an old response cannot spend the replacement snapshot's budget |
| #6739 | 2026-11-14_keepalive-rotated-timers | #6737 | credential rotation deleted the registry entry but never cancelled the scheduled ping — the dropped snapshot stayed referenced until its old cadence fired → `disarm(..., "credential-rotated")` |
| #6738 | 2026-11-14_cache-diff-insertion-boundaries | #6736 | cache-diff "mid-insert append" misclassified inserting a WHOLE message between existing ones as a semantic append (byte shape is identical) → require same element count with exactly one span growing by the insertion; growth before the root array now reports preArray divergence |
| #6742 | 2026-11-14_usage-log-attribution-tags | #6740 | usage-log parsing attributed samples to the new logger's `[v=]`/`[sess=]` tags (or a request scope) instead of the explicit session → strip logger tags, require the session tag directly before `[acp-usage]`, never invent one |
| #6743 | 2026-11-14_nested-upstream-error-codes | #6741 | upstream alert errno extraction only read the outer `error.code` — native fetch failures nest the errno in `cause` → walk the cause chain (depth-capped, cycle-safe), outer nonempty code keeps precedence |
| #6747 | 2026-11-14_linear-fold-registration | #6744 | batch fold registration re-scanned the whole fold list to close open records per block (O(folds×blocks)) → closeFrom cursor; batch/individual parity kept |
| #6748 | 2026-11-14_linear-handoff-capture | #6746 | handoff reply metering re-encapsulated the entire accumulated text on every delta (O(n²)) → incremental byte accounting with surrogate-pair junction correction; exact UTF-8 budget boundaries kept |
| #6750 | 2026-11-14_diagnostics-unicode-bounds | #6749 | diagnostics truncation used plain `slice`, which can split a surrogate pair at the bound → `safePrefix` everywhere the bound applies (log tails, config, conflict detail, topic) |

Verification (clean checkout of this branch, node 22.23.4, CI preload chain):
- per-PR added-line audit vs its merge-base: all 11 clean
- `tsc --noEmit`: clean
- all 11 touched test files: 187 pass

After this merges, the 11 source PRs become branch ancestors of master and close with their Closes keywords.

Closes #6724 #6726 #6732 #6734 #6736 #6737 #6740 #6741 #6744 #6746 #6749
